stories.headline: US and Iran hold first talks since June amid escalating rhetoric at the UN

sources.body:
Top Iranian and US officials have held talks at the UN in New York on a day when the US leader said he could "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if the conflict went unresolved.

No breakthrough has been reported from the meeting mediated by Qatar and involving Iran's foreign minister and US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff - the first since a June ceasefire unravelled.

Witkoff said a round of discussions had been completed "that we hope will prove constructive and promising". Iran repeated its demand for the US to end its "acts of aggression".

The US and Israel launched air strikes on Iran on 28 February. Iran responded by attacking Israel and US bases in the Gulf and Arab Gulf allies of the US - as well as blocking the Strait of Hormuz.

Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to pass through the strait before the war and its closure has caused wild fluctuations of prices.

It has also increased pressure on Trump to find a way of ending the conflict - particularly as the US heads to Congressional elections in November.

In his address at the annual meeting of the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, Trump began by touting his accomplishments on the economy, immigration, the border and tackling violent crime - remarks that sounded more pitched to voters the US midterms than the diplomats in the hall.

He spent much of his address justifying the war with Iran - a huge contrast with remarks earlier by UN Secretary General António Guterres, who warned global divisions were deepening and underscored the "interdependence" of the world's peoples.

The US president argued that the conflict had prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and demonstrated the value of what he described as peace through strength - ultimatums rather than deal-making or compromise.

"Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?" he said.

"Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again? Do I drive them into hell?"

Trump said he believed an Iran deal, which has so far eluded him, would come right after November's elections.

The remarks were indicative of his foreign-policy strategy of coercive diplomacy - threatening overwhelming force while keeping negotiations open.

Trump later told reporters that American officials had had a "very productive" three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation on the sidelines of the general assembly.

Iran state TV confirmed that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had met Witkoff.

Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei, quoted by state broadcaster IRNA, later said negotiations took part through a Qatari mediator who communicated Tehran's conditions, including an end to the war on all fronts and to US "acts of aggression".

The BBC asked Witkoff how the meetings had gone as he was leaving the UN building and he responded with a thumbs up. Witkoff later confirmed on X that the talks had been held "through the mediators, who shuttled between the two sides throughout the day".
sources.headline: US and Iran hold first talks since June after Trump's 'annihilation' threat

sources.body:
Senior Iranian official indicates willingness to reopen strait of Hormuz if US takes steps to ease pressure on Tehran

Iranian officials held three hours of talks with US special envoy Steve Witkoff on the sidelines of the UN general assembly, Donald Trump disclosed on Tuesday.

He said there would a further meeting in the very near future.

Witkoff said he felt very good about the meeting, the first such contact since the US vice-president, JD Vance, met an Iranian delegation to agree a memorandum of understanding in Switzerland in June .

Iranian officials confirmed the meeting with Witkoff involved its foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, and was mediated by diplomats from Qatar.

A senior Iranian official also indicated that the country was prepared to reopen the strait of Hormuz within a week, as long as the US took reciprocal steps to ease the military and economic pressure it is applying on Iran.

Previously, Iran had set seven onerous preconditions for lifting its blockade on the strait, one of the world’s key oil shipping routes, including an end to the US war “on all fronts” and a commitment by the US to end all aggressive actions against Iran, including sanctions.

The new position, revealed amid frantic backstage negotiations at the UN general assembly in New York and set out by an Iranian official in Tehran to the Japanese news agency Kyodo and then to Reuters, would involve relaxing some of those preconditions.

The official claimed the position had been approved by Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei , and the country’s supreme national security council, although some Iranian media close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) denied any new position had been adopted, reflecting disputes in Tehran.

Diplomats had been testing the ground for possible talks between the US and Iran, with Qatar’s diplomats in talks with Araghchi. A meeting between Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, and Trump had largely been ruled out as too combustible, however.

Pezeshkian is due on Wednesday to address the UN general assembly, where most of the Iranian delegation left the hall during Trump’s speech on Tuesday after he described Iran as the bully of the Middle East and the number one terror organisation on Earth.

But earlier, the IRGC issued a statement that said there was no contradiction between staging negotiations and waging war at the same time, a position echoed by Iran’s chief negotiator , Mohammad Ghalibaf, in recent remarks delivered online to the Iranian parliament.

The official said Iran was seeking signs from Washington that it was prepared to return to negotiations and take steps toward ending its military blockade of Iranian ports and halting military operations related to the strait of Hormuz. In that case, Iran was prepared to reopen the strategic waterway within seven days and return to the negotiating table, according to the official.

Such preconditions are less stringent than those issued by other senior Iranian figures in the previous 48 hours.
sources.headline: Iran and US have held talks on sidelines of UN summit, says Donald Trump

sources.body:
Tehran ties diplomatic progress to lifting shipping blockades and unfreezing assets during New York negotiations.

The United States and Iran have engaged in hours of indirect talks through mediators on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, but accounts differed over whether officials from the two countries met directly.

US special envoy Steve Witkoff said mediators had “shuttled between” the American and Iranian delegations throughout Tuesday.

“Today, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, we engaged in lengthy talks with the Iranian delegation through the mediators, who shuttled between the two sides throughout the day,” Witkoff said in a post on X.

“They successfully completed a round of discussions that we hope will prove constructive and promising. The mediators will continue their work.”

US President Donald Trump gave a more direct account, saying Witkoff and Jared Kushner had held a three-hour meeting with Iranian officials.

“They had a very good meeting, a very productive meeting,” Trump told reporters at the UN, adding that he believed there was “a lot of momentum” towards an agreement. Trump later said talks were continuing and that he believed a settlement would eventually be reached.

Al Jazeera’s Kimberly Halkett, reporting from Washington, said Trump’s initial comments had created confusion over who had participated. She said the White House later clarified that Trump had not attended and that Witkoff and Kushner represented the US side.

Al Jazeera’s Tohid Asadi, reporting from Tehran, said state media had confirmed a meeting between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Witkoff after weeks without direct contact.

“This latest meeting was held at the request and insistence of the American side, and was aimed at conveying Iran’s messages and conditions, particularly around reopening the Strait of Hormuz,” Asadi reported.

Iranian state media said those conditions included lifting the US naval blockade, releasing frozen Iranian assets and ending the war on what Tehran describes as the “resistance” fronts.

Asadi also reported that an Iranian security source told Al Jazeera there could be room for further diplomatic engagement if Washington met Iran’s conditions and commitments.

The contacts came after a senior Iranian official told the Reuters news agency that Tehran’s delegation in New York had full authority to pursue diplomacy and described the UN gathering as a “golden opportunity” for Washington to return to negotiations.

The official said Iran had submitted its latest proposal to Washington through mediators on September 16 and that details of a possible agreement to end hostilities could be discussed in New York.

The official also said Iran could reopen Hormuz within seven days if the US eased military pressure and lifted its blockade of Iranian ports.

The indirect talks have been accompanied by a broader diplomatic effort involving the Gulf and other regional states.

Qatar said it was working with Pakistan to reduce tensions between Washington and Tehran, safeguard freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and promote regional stability.
sources.headline: US, Iran hold mediated UNGA talks on ending war, opening Strait of Hormuz

stories.headline: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready for an energy ceasefire with Russia ahead of winter

sources.body: On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told journalists that Kyiv is ready to halt strikes on Russian energy infrastructure if Moscow does the same, with hopes to end the war before winter.
sources.headline: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready for an energy ceasefire with Russia

sources.body:
Zelenskyy says Kyiv and Washington discussed an energy ceasefire, air defences and steps towards ending Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said Kyiv remains ready for a bilateral “energy ceasefire” with Russia after holding separate talks with the leaders of the United States and the United Kingdom in New York City.

He also warned in a post on Telegram on Tuesday that Russia was planning “a new massive attack” against his country.

Zelenskyy, who was in New York for the United Nations General Assembly, met with US President Donald Trump for 40 minutes and said the talks focused on efforts to end Russia’s full-scale invasion of his country, now in its fifth year.

Writing on X, he said the talks were “positive and productive”.

“Both the US and Ukraine want to see this senseless Russian war ended before winter. We discussed potential de-escalatory steps that can open up the way to diplomacy,” he added.

In comments to reporters at the UN headquarters in New York, Zelenskyy said Kyiv remains ready to halt strikes on Russian energy facilities if Moscow stops targeting Ukraine’s energy system. But he stressed that there had been no discussion with Trump of Kyiv unilaterally ending attacks on the Russian oil industry.

“We are ready for energy ceasefire,” he said. “If they don’t want us to attack their diesel and refineries, and etc, we are ready – if they will not attack our energy system, our electricity, heating system, water supplies.”

Trump, whose approval ratings have slumped to a record low amid high petrol prices ahead of the US midterm elections in November, had expressed concern in recent days over the extensive damage done by Ukraine to Russia’s fuel-processing capacity, which he said was stoking diesel prices globally.

Before the meeting, Trump told reporters that he and Zelenskyy would discuss Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries.

“It is a serious hit on the Russians. It’s also a serious hit on the price of diesel,” Trump said.

He said they would also talk about solutions for ending the war, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. “I think it’s going to happen,” he added.

The US president said last week that the two countries had agreed to stop attacking each other’s energy facilities, but strikes resumed almost immediately.

The Kremlin had previously welcomed the US proposal for an energy moratorium while also calling for measures covering Russian seaborne energy exports and sanctions.

But Zelenskyy, writing on Telegram following his meeting with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, said there could not possibly be any discussion of easing sanctions against Russia “when Ukrainians live every day under the threat of missile and drone attacks”.

“There’s intelligence right now that Russia is preparing a new ⁠massive attack against Ukraine,” he wrote.

The renewed push for an energy ceasefire comes after weeks of intensifying long-range attacks by both sides. Russia has repeatedly targeted Ukraine’s power, fuel and port infrastructure, raising fears of further damage to the country’s energy system as temperatures fall. On September 15, Russia launched about 200 drones across Ukraine, according to Ukrainian officials, hitting petrol stations in Kyiv as well as energy and port infrastructure elsewhere.
sources.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine ready for energy truce with Russia after Trump talks

stories.headline: US agrees with Denmark to expand its military presence in Greenland

sources.body:
The US, Denmark and Greenland have signed a defence deal that allows Washington to build two new military bases in the Arctic territory, while reaffirming Copenhagen's sovereignty over it.

Before a signing ceremony at the UN General Assembly in New York, US President Donald Trump said "we will immediately begin the process of developing a large military presence in the appropriate locations".

Danish PM Mette Frederiksen said the deal was "good for the US, Denmark and Greenland" and also for Europe and Nato, while Greenland's PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen said it was a "win-win-win".

The three leaders then inked the deal, seemingly ending more than a year of tension over the Arctic territory.

Trump had threatened to "take" the semi-autonomous Arctic territory over what he said were national security concerns, citing its strategic defence location and its mineral wealth.

His rhetoric prompted outcry from Greenlanders, Danes and European leaders who issued a joint statement saying his words "undermine transatlantic relations and risk a dangerous downward spiral".

The deal amends and updates a 1951 defence agreement between Denmark and the US.

The new pact says the US "shall be allowed to establish an additional Defence Area at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig" - referring to locations in Greenland's south and east.

Narsarsuaq is a former civilian airport and World War Two base. It has deep-water access and a large runway which US military engineers were recently surveying, the US North Command confirmed to the BBC.

The Mestersvig outpost is remote, far less developed, and used by a Danish naval dog sled unit.

The "modalities and technical details" of the bases are yet to be confirmed, and according to the deal, must be mutually agreed by all parties,

This means the US security arrangements are not unfettered and Greenland and Denmark's approval is still needed.

Washington currently operates its Pituffik Space Base in Greenland's north-west, and the new deal allows the US to "modernise and expand its activities" there.

It also says that "no state that is not a member of Nato shall be allowed to establish its own manned or unmanned military installations in Greenland nor shall they be allowed a persistent presence of military forces in Greenland".

Although the militaries of non-Nato countries are now explicitly barred from the island, it was highly unlikely that non-allied troops would have been allowed access in the first place.

Critically, no territory is ceded to the US, and it recognises both Denmark's "sovereignty and territorial integrity" and Greenland's right to self-determination.

On one hand, that's a significant climb down from Trump's earlier calls to acquire the Arctic island.

But it does deliver a strengthened US military presence and expand on the previous agreement. Therefore to some American eyes, that will be perceived as a historic win.

The new deal must still be approved by both Denmark's and Greenland's parliaments.

Despite months of crisis, the mood at Tuesday's signing ceremony appeared strikingly upbeat and friendly.
sources.headline: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark

sources.body:
At least two new US bases will be established as part of a deal with Denmark and Greenland.

The US will open two military bases in Greenland as part of a deal with Denmark and Greenland, Reuters has reported.

The agreement is expected to be signed on Tuesday at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. However, its text has not yet been officially publicised.

The move follows a tense, months-long standoff with Denmark and Greenland following US President Donald Trump’s repeated comments that Washington intended to annex the autonomous Danish territory, which is strategic for its location in the Arctic and its significant mineral resources, including rare-earth metals.

As a diplomatic row brewed last year, Trump refused to rule out a military invasion, causing fear among Greenlanders, the majority of whom reject US control according to polls.

Tensions peaked in January this year when European members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) alliance began deploying more troops to the island to demonstrate military readiness and to deter Washington.

Following talks with NATO chief Mark Rutte, Trump backed down, saying he would not invade the island but would, instead, work towards a deal. He also withdrew his threat to impose 10 percent trade tariffs on eight European nations objecting to the US’s attempts to acquire Greenland.

Greenland and Denmark then began negotiations with the US to de-escalate the crisis. Here’s what we know:

On Friday, US President Donald Trump claimed the US had reached a deal with Denmark granting it “permanent control” over Greenland’s security “and all other needs”.

The deal allows the US a veto to prevent “adversaries” from establishing a military presence or making “sensitive investments” in Greenland without its approval, Trump said.

A US Department of State official cited by the BBC clarified that will mean non-NATO states will not be able to set up bases in Greenland and will be barred from “making investments in Greenland that could threaten the United States”.

Then, on Monday, news of the two new US bases emerged.

Over the weekend, Denmark and Greenland confirmed they had reached an agreement with the US that would be announced this week, but insisted that it would not compromise Greenland’s sovereignty.

In a post on Facebook, Greenland’s Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said, “The agreement recognises the sovereignty and territorial integrity of our kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination.”

On Monday, in advance of the deal’s signing, Nielsen added that it would be a “significant moment following a difficult period … I look forward to signing the agreement and taking the next step with our interests, our security, and respect for our country as the clear starting point.”

Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen also sounded an optimistic note in a weekend statement.

“A time of uncertainty will hopefully give way to a binding agreement that strengthens security ‌in the Arctic and the north Atlantic, and thereby our shared security within Nato Europe – while respecting the Danish kingdom’s red lines,” Rasmussen said.
sources.headline: Where is the US opening new military bases in Greenland?

stories.headline: EU removes Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its Russia sanctions list

sources.body:
Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman delisted in what Ireland’s EU presidency calls ‘a difficult compromise’ for the bloc

The EU has agreed to remove two Russian billionaires, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, from its sanctions list, while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 individuals and companies accused of supporting the war on Ukraine for the next three years.

With an end-of-Tuesday deadline looming to preserve the Russia blacklist, the EU’s 27 member states found a compromise that meant delisting the two oligarchs in spite of very few countries wanting this outcome. EU sanctions have to be approved unanimously.

France stunned and infuriated EU governments this month when it called for Usmanov, a Russian-Uzbek national, to be removed from the list on “national security” grounds, reported to refer to a prisoner exchange deal involving French nationals and Azerbaijan.

Luxembourg then asked for the same treatment for Fridman, the Russian-Israeli magnate, who is suing the Grand Duchy for $16bn (£12bn) for freezing his assets.

The exemptions angered many EU countries which believe it sets a bad precedent by allowing member states to weaken sanctions in defence of national interests.

Ukraine criticised the removal of the men from the sanctions list as unacceptable. Shortly after the decision emerged, Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, wrote on social media: “No name on the sanctions list is there by accident: each one represents a reason why this war started and continues to this day.”

The Ukrainian foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, called the decision “shameful and unjustifiable” on X. “Moscow is celebrating because it got what it wanted: a sense ‌of impunity, the humiliation of the EU, and division among Europeans,” he added.

In order to enable the delistings that many EU member states found unpalatable, it was proposed that the sanctions be rolled over for 36 months, rather than the usual six.

A spokesperson for Ireland’s EU presidency, which brokered the talks, said the bloc had reached “a difficult compromise”. They said: “Until now, these listings have been reviewed and assessed on a six-monthly basis; today’s decision to renew on a 36-month basis enhances the durability and predictability of the EU sanctions framework.”

A decision had been expected earlier this week, but Latvia’s government, facing parliamentary elections on 3 October, announced a last-minute objection to the delistings on Monday. Latvia’s prime minister, Andris Kulbergs, said late on Monday night that he could not accept the proposed compromise and instructed his foreign minister to enter talks with Paris and Brussels to find a solution.

Diplomats said Latvia had finally agreed to abstain on the two delistings. The blacklist includes Russia’s president, Vladimir Putin, and foreign minister, Sergey Lavrov, as well as Duma deputies, the country’s major banks, energy companies and military industrial complex.

Senior EU officials have promised to present about 1,600 new designations – individuals and entities involved in the Russian military industrial complex – to foreign ministers next month. But the latest standoff, which followed the tortuous agreement on the EU’s 21st round of sanctions in July, suggests the process could be difficult.
sources.headline: EU removes two oligarchs from Russia sanctions list as deadline looms

stories.headline: Hurricane Polo rapidly intensifies into a Category 5 storm off Mexico

sources.body:
Hurricane Polo has rapidly intensified off the coast of Mexico to become one of the most powerful storms of the season in the Pacific Ocean.

A Hurricane Hunter aircraft, operated by the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), flew into the storm on Tuesday and recorded sustained wind speeds near 180 mph (285 km/h), with stronger gusts.

NOAA's Miami-based National Hurricane Center called the storm "extremely dangerous" and said its intensification over 24 hours was "truly remarkable".

The slow-moving storm is fuelling up on extremely warm waters caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon and is the season's third category 5 storm, the highest level on the Saffir-Simpson scale.

The storm is predicted to skirt the coast of south-western Mexico, but is not expected to make landfall, a warning from NOAA said.

As it slowly drifts northwest, Polo will drive torrential rainfall in parts of Mexico's south-west coast - which could lead to deadly flooding and mudslides, NOAA said.

Rainfall totals of up to 6in (15cm) are forecast, with 8in possible in some areas. Residents have also been warned of large ocean swells and life-threatening surf conditions for the next few days.

"So far, the information we have is that (Polo) will not make a direct landfall on the coast," Mexico's President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Tuesday, but she warned residents along the Pacific coast to be vigilant. Sheinbaum highlighted the states of Jalisco, Colima and Michoacan as being at risk.

Data from the Hurricane Hunter aircraft indicated that Polo could still strengthen and would likely stay a category 5 storm for the next few days, because of what NOAA called a "very conducive" environment of extremely warm ocean waters feeding the storm.

Scientists monitoring the ocean temperatures say the current El Niño climate phenomenon is now the strongest on record.

Daily sea surface temperatures in a key region of the central-eastern Pacific were 3.05C above average on 19 September - exceeding the previous record of 3.02C set during the very strong El Niño of 2015.

Some longer-term measures of El Niño have not yet hit record levels but this is likely to change, with the peak not expected until later this year.

Warmer ocean waters mean storms can pick up more energy, leading to higher wind speeds.

El Niño is a naturally-occurring pattern, which happens about every two to seven years and tends to last for around a year.

Trade winds that typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean can weaken or even reverse, allowing warm water to spread eastwards.

Heat is then released from the ocean into the atmosphere which can boost global temperatures and drive changes in weather patterns around the world.
sources.headline: Hurricane Polo intensifies into rare category 5 storm off the coast of Mexico

sources.body:
Polo, with sustained winds of 165mph, is churning 215 miles south of Zihuatanejo but is unlikely to directly hit Mexico

A tropical storm off the south-west coast of Mexico has intensified into a category 5 monster in fewer than 24 hours, fueled by stronger than usual El Niño weather patterns in the Pacific Ocean.

Hurricane Polo was sending out maximum sustained winds of 165mph (266km/h) on Tuesday as its center churned about 215 miles (346km) south of the coastal city of Zihuatanejo, in Guerrero state.

On Monday, Polo was only a tropical storm with winds below 74mph (120km/h). Its rapid and sudden growth is testament to the dominance of this year’s so-called super El Niño, which set a record on Monday as the most extreme on record , and has amplified a number of extreme weather events globally.

Forecasters at the National Hurricane Center in Miami said Mexico was likely to avoid a direct hit, but warned that further intensification was likely, and that life-threatening flooding and mudslides were possible inland, along with dangerous surf and rip current conditions.

El Niño occurs when extended ocean temperatures in the eastern and central Pacific, and near the equator, rise above their historical average.

Meteorologists say the phenomenon increases disruptive winds and curtails other conditions favorable to storm development in the Atlantic basin, which remains quiet with less than three months to go in this year’s hurricane season.

Conversely, it promotes increased activity in the Pacific, where the 2026 El Niño remains one of the strongest on record.

“The water temperatures in two separate areas, the north-central Pacific and off the Mexican coast, are running well above average,” Paul Pastelok, AccuWeather’s lead long-range meteorologist, said in the online weather service’s fall hurricane outlook last month.

“We are seeing a strong impact in both the Atlantic and Pacific basins, with extreme wind shear limiting Atlantic storm development, while the Pacific remains quite active, as we expected back in the spring.”

Hurricane Polo’s single-day intensification also fits into the assessment of University of Miami senior research associate Brian McNoldy on his tropical Atlantic blog that El Niño, which he said was only “moderate” towards the beginning of September, was “forecast to become very strong, likely the strongest on record, by later this fall and into winter”.

Polo is the 18th named storm, and seventh hurricane, of the 2026 Pacific season, which runs from 15 May until 30 November.

By contrast, the Atlantic basin, which has a six-month season from June until November, has seen only six named tropical storms and no hurricanes so far.

It is the first time in 112 years that no Atlantic hurricanes have formed by 21 September, and 2026 could join 1907 and 1914 as the only years without one being recorded.
sources.headline: Hurricane Polo, rapidly intensifying from strong El Niño patterns, rages off coast of Mexico

stories.headline: Republican Senate candidates break with Trump and call for a quick end to the Iran war

sources.body: Sen. Jon Husted became the latest battleground Republican this week to call for a quick end to the Iran war, as panic grows over how high gas prices and President Donald Trump’s agenda could imperil the party’s chances in November. “The war needs to come to an end as quickly as possible so that we can lower gas prices,” the Ohio senator told POLITICO, in his furthest comments yet on the matter. Coming after Iowa Senate nominee Ashley Hinson, who broke from Trump over the war on Monday , and Michigan Senate nominee Mike Rogers , who followed suit hours later, Husted’s comments are another example of the pressure he and other Republicans are under to address prices at the pump. Several candidates are creating some distance from Trump, as voters continue to blame the president for the current economy and the Iran conflict for high costs of living. Husted said in the interview that he still thinks Iran needs to reach a deal with Trump to end the conflict, but added: “I don’t know anybody that doesn’t want the war to come to an end.” He has a finer line to walk with Trump in his state, and Republicans close to him say he can’t and won't completely break with the president. Husted does not plan to support the Democratic-led war powers resolution when it comes up for a vote in the Senate this week, a spokesperson said. And Trump and Vice President JD Vance are expected to visit the state in the coming weeks to shore up his campaign and drive GOP turnout. Husted is staring down a tight race against former Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown, where millions in spending and recent polling have put Brown slightly ahead. Top Hill Republicans and Senate GOP operatives have said the Ohio Senate race is among their primary concerns in the battle to keep control of the chamber. But Ohio is just one in a series of battlegrounds where rising gas prices have become a defining issue. Beyond Hinson and Rogers, a growing number of Republicans are starting to call for emergency actions like a diesel export ban to lower gas prices, including Iowa GOP Reps. Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks. “Hinson broke the dam,” said one GOP operative, who was granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. Sen. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), who is locked in an incredibly competitive race, called Tuesday for a diesel export ban to provide voters relief. He didn’t mention the Iran war. The panic is being felt most acutely in the Midwest, as high gas and diesel prices and Trump’s tariffs hammer families, truckers and farmers just a few weeks ahead of the peak harvest season with no relief in sight. By Sunday night, Rogers had filmed an ad at a grocery store decrying high prices and, straight to camera, breaking with Trump to call for an end to the Iran war, according to two Republicans involved in the matter, granted anonymity to discuss internal conversations. Rogers’ team was putting the finishing touches on the ad Monday morning when Hinson posted her break with Trump over the war directly on social media. “The war’s just gone on too long. Mike still thinks Iran shouldn’t have a nuclear weapon, but we originally thought this would take six weeks,” said one person with direct knowledge of the conversations in Rogers’ camp about the move. “Voters have been paying for it at their kitchen tables for too long.” Michigan’s GOP nominee for governor, Rep. John James, also said Tuesday the Iran war needs to end “quickly.” And Rep. Tom Tiffany, Wisconsin’s GOP governor nominee, said Tuesday he believes “we should be exiting Iran, that it’s time to move on, we’ve degraded their nuclear facilities, we’ve degraded their military … time to come home, take care of business here in America.” Trump, for his part, told reporters Tuesday that he asked his team to consider a diesel export ban, and that his administration is mulling it. But the move is rife with internal GOP fighting behind the scenes: Trump’s team is getting an earful from GOP lawmakers in oil states who oppose the move, according to four people with direct knowledge of the matter who were granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. That makes any decision before the midterms highly problematic with at least one corner of the party. Both the top House GOP leaders — Speaker Mike Johnson and Majority Leader Steve Scalise — have opposed similar measures from the past to protect their oil state of Louisiana. The Texas GOP delegation is also “strongly opposed,” according to another Republican. Husted told POLITICO on Tuesday that he supports his state legislature suspending Ohio’s gas tax for a period. Democrat Amy Acton, who is running for governor, called for a gas tax suspension Monday . Her GOP opponent Vivek Ramaswamy and a broader swath of Republicans called for the state legislature to convene and pass legislation to suspend the state’s gas tax hours later. “I think in the long run we are going to have lower gas prices,” Husted said, citing the war in Ukraine as a factor for spiking diesel costs as well as the war with Iran. “It's taking longer than any of us wish it would. So in the interim, while those things are concluding, the idea of providing relief from the gas tax for Ohioans for a short period of time is a reasonable thing for Governor [Mike] DeWine to consider.”
sources.headline: Sen. Jon Husted: Iran war ‘needs to come to an end as quickly as possible’

sources.body:
The US Supreme Court has refused to intervene in a custody dispute involving a surrogate who refused an abortion request from the parents who hired her to have their baby.

Justice Elena Kagan declined an emergency appeal filed by McKenna West asking the court to halt a previous ruling granting parental rights to the California couple.

The parents had asked West to abort the pregnancy after a scan at 20 weeks showed the foetus had a severe heart defect. West instead went to Texas where nearly all abortions are illegal and gave birth to the child.

The court's decision leaves in place an earlier order that granted custody to the parents.

The BBC has contacted lawyers for both parties for comment.

West has been seeking custody over the baby, which was born last month with hypoplastic left heart syndrome - a defect where the left side of the heart cannot pump enough blood to the body.

The condition often requires multiple surgeries, which are not a cure. Infants with the condition can have lifelong complications, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

West - who has been supported by several Republican officials - travelled to Texas, where the state's Attorney General Ken Paxton intervened in the case and won an emergency court order requiring that the boy receive medical care in the state. He had surgery soon after birth.

West said she denied the parents', Omar Ahmed and Nausheen Gilkar, requests to have the abortion after learning of treatment options and wanting to keep "this precious baby", according to the Supreme Court filing.

West argued that the biological parents should not have custody because she worried they would not give the boy the necessary medical care since they sought to abort the child after learning of the life-threatening condition.

In a previous court hearing, Gilkar said the baby - whom they named Rumi - was "our child" and "the love of our lives", according to the Associated Press. They said West travelled to Texas without telling them and blocked their access to medical information.

A California court previously granted parental rights to Ahmed and Gilkar, while a Texas court issued a restraining order blocking West from seeing the baby.

Last month, an attorney for the California couple said the child was in critical condition and seemed to be "suffering from potential complications".

West argued that without intervention from the Supreme Court, she would no longer have access to information about the child's medical condition.

In the filing, lawyers for West suggested that the California couple could place the child in hospice care.
sources.headline: Supreme Court stays out of custody case involving surrogate who refused abortion

stories.headline: Spain presses Morocco for answers over the Ceuta border-control failure

sources.body: <p>El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha apuntado esta vez con mucha claridad a la responsabilidad de Marruecos en el fallo del control de la frontera con la ciudad de Ceuta el pasado 30 y 31 de julio y a la necesidad de corregirla. Sánchez ha asegurado que España ha pedido a Rabat medidas urgentes para resolver este problema. Las declaraciones las ha hecho en Nueva York, en una entrevista con la CNN. Preguntado por la crisis de Ceuta, que la periodista Christiane Amanpour ha calificado de “desastre”, ha reivindicado la buena relación con Rabat pero también ha dicho que España ha “pedido respuestas y acciones a Marruecos porque es evidente que su control de la frontera falló”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-22/sanchez-pide-explicaciones-a-marruecos-porque-su-control-de-fronteras-fallo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Sánchez asegura que ha pedido “acciones” a Marruecos “porque su control de fronteras falló” en Ceuta

sources.body:
El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez , ha responsabilizado a Marruecos por primera vez desde la entrada masiva de más de 80.000 inmigrantes en Ceuta el pasado 30 de julio. Casi dos meses después, en una entrevista en la CNN , Sánchez ha asegurado que "ha pedido a Marruecos respuestas y acciones porque está claro que su mecanismo de control fronterizo falló".

Según Sánchez, "seguridad y orden se pueden garantizar sin que sea a costa de la dignidad humana" y apunta al país marroquí. "Tenemos que tener una relación positiva con Marruecos y tenemos una unión estratégica con ellos por que tenemos que devolverlos a su país de origen que es Marruecos. Lo devolveremos con dignidad porque en España los inmigrantes no son ganado sino humanos", ha añadido Sánchez desde Nueva York.

En su comparecencia ante el Congreso de los Diputados el 3 de septiembre, Sánchez mantuvo que no había pruebas de que Marruecos planificara o ejecutara la entrada masiva en Ceuta. Y ha advirtió de que si hay evidencias sólidas contra Rabat, el Gobierno actuaría "con contundencia". Lo hizo un día después de conocerse el informe aportado por la Policía a la jueza de la Audiencia Nacional María Tardón, en el que se señalaba a las fuerzas de seguridad de Marruecos como responsables de una llegada masiva de personas, que fue "planificada ", en ningún caso "espontánea".

La entrevista se ha producido el primer día del presidente en Nueva York para asistir a la Asamblea de la ONU.

La jornada ha estado marcada, asimismo, por la ausencia de Sánchez —"por motivos de agenda, según la Moncloa— a la recepción de líderes que ofrece el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump . También por el saludo de la presidenta interina de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez , que se ha acercado expresamente a Sánchez durante la reunión de la ONU.

Rodríguez ha pedido seguir hablando de la situación en el país sudamericano y el presidente se ha mostrado comprometido con el futuro de la región, según fuentes de Moncloa. Por el momento, no hay previsto ningún encuentro más entre ambos mandatarios.

En una entrevista con Jon Stewart para el programa The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart , de la que se ha difundido este martes un adelanto a través de X, Sánchez ha calificado de "ideológico" y " no respaldado por hechos y datos " el discurso pronunciado este martes por Trump ante la Asamblea General de la ONU, en el que cuestionó el cambio climático y amenazó con "aniquilar" Irán si no alcanza un acuerdo para poner fin a la guerra.

"Creo que fue un discurso muy ideológico, no respaldado por hechos y datos", ha afirmado Sánchez, que se ha referido a las posiciones expresadas por Trump sobre el cambio climático, la guerra en Irán y la situación en Oriente Medio, y ha sostenido que las del mandatario estadounidense "no están, digamos, ampliamente respaldadas por muchos países en todo el mundo".

Trump dedicó buena parte de su intervención ante los líderes mundiales a defender la política exterior de su Administración y, en particular, su decisión de entrar en guerra con Irán.

Migrantes en chabolas, en la playa de Trampolín en Ceuta. / Marcos Moreno / Europa Press

El Gobierno comenzará a enviar a Marruecos en los próximos días los primeros expedientes de los menores migrantes en Ceuta -tras el 30 de julio- para consultar sobre las posibilidades respecto a su reagrupación familiar. Ahora mismo hay 2.321 menores filiados en total, sumando tanto los que entraron el 30 y 31 de julio como los días previos, además de entre 700 y 1.000 que, según los cálculos del Ejecutivo, siguen en las calles. Desde el Ejecutivo siempre destacaron públicamente la voluntad expresada por Rabat de colaborar para su repatriación, pero en los últimos días se han ido elevando las dudas. La realidad es que de los 600 expedientes enviados antes de la entrada masiva todavía no se ha tenido ningún tipo de respuesta. Fuentes del Ejecutivo reconocen así que la “experiencia” les hace ser cautos.

El compromiso trasmitido por Rabat al Gobierno y también por carta a algunos europarlamentarios para facilitar las repatriaciones se circunscribe a los menores que cruzaron a Ceuta durante la entrada masiva de finales de julio. La intención del Gobierno, sin embargo, es enviar un primer “lote” de expedientes para consultar sobre la reagrupación familiar priorizando “los más vulnerables”, sin diferenciar sus fechas de entrada.

"No suele ser habitual que tengamos una respuesta fluida de Marruecos y esto suele ser un problema", avisaba la ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego , ante el envío inminente de las solicitudes para la reagrupación familiar. Otras fuentes del mando único para Ceuta destacan que se trabajará con Marruecos en este sentido. Estos días, precisamente, está previsto que el ministro de Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, se reúna con su homólogo marroquí, Nasser Bourita , en los márgenes de la semana de alto nivel de Naciones Unidas en Nueva York para abordar el retorno de los migrantes que permanecen en Ceuta, tanto mayores como menores.

Desde el pasado 1 de agosto, se han reagrupado a 54 menores con sus familias en la Península, según datos del departamento de Juventud e Infancia, a través del procedimiento de urgencia . Todos ellos entraron solos en la "avalancha" entre los días 30 y 31 de julio.

Para su reagrupación se siguió el procedimiento habitual cuando las familias reclaman el reagrupamiento y se demuestra el vínculo familiar. Para ello es necesario que el familiar acuda a Ceuta a su recogida y la Policía autorizar su salida tras la acreditación del vínculo. Ceuta, por su parte, informa a Fiscalía y a los servicios sociales de la comunidad de destino.

La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego. / Marta Fernández / Europa Press

Según fuentes del ministerio de Juventud e Infancia, se encuentran abiertos más de 300 expedientes de reagrupamiento familiar en Península. En el caso de los reagrupamientos familiares en el país de origen, reconocen desde este departamento, "los plazos se pueden extender durante meses ya que conlleva la implicación de distintas administraciones y autoridades extranjeras".

stories.headline: OECD raises Spain's 2026 growth forecast to 2.6% but warns inflation will remain above the European average

sources.body:
El secretario general de la OCDE, Mathias Cormann 

Pese a las incertidumbres que está viviendo la economía global, golpeada por un shock energético a gran escala, España sigue portándose mejor que el resto de sus homólogos europeos. La Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económico (OCDE) ha mejorado este miércoles cuatro décimas hasta el 2,6% respecto a sus cálculos del pasado mes de junio. Es una tasa que supera el promedio de la eurozona, que es ligeramente inferior a la del 2025 (un 2,8%) y que está en línea con el dato que maneja el Gobierno.

No obstante, la institución con sede en París advierte que parte de este incremento será exclusivamente nominal, porque se verá acompañado por un alza sustancial de la tasa de inflación, que se ha actualizado hasta un 3,7%, también cuatro décimas de lo que se previo inicialmente.

“Varias economías europeas, en particular el Reino Unido y España, experimentaron asimismo un sólido crecimiento de la demanda interna en el segundo trimestre, mientras que la recuperación de las exportaciones respaldó el repunte en Alemania”, indicó el organismo.

De cara al año siguiente, la OCDE ha elevado una décima el crecimiento del PIB para el 2027 hasta el 1,8%, gracias a la fuerza de la demanda interna y estima que la inflación alcanzará un 3,4%, cinco décimas más que el último estudio, debido al encarecimiento de la energía en los mercados internacionales.

En La Vanguardia desde el 2000. Especializado en Economía internacional, ha cubierto como enviado el Foro Económico de Davos, la OMC o el BCE. Licenciado en Derecho en Roma, Master en Periodismo UB/, PDD del IESE. Premio AECOC.
sources.headline: La OCDE revisa al alza cuatro décimas el crecimiento de España este año hasta el 2,6%

sources.body:
industria automovil coches neomotor fabrica coche automocion (4) / Agencias

La economía española afrontará los próximos meses con un ritmo de crecimiento superior al que se esperaba hace apenas unos meses, aunque con la inflación como principal foco de preocupación. La Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económicos (OCDE) ha revisado al alza su previsión de crecimiento para España en 2026 hasta el 2,6%, cuatro décimas por encima de la estimación que manejaba en junio. El organismo sitúa así a España entre las economías europeas con una evolución más favorable, en un escenario internacional condicionado por la escalada de las tensiones en Oriente Próximo y la elevada volatilidad de los mercados energéticos.

La mejora de las perspectivas económicas contrasta, sin embargo, con la resistencia de los precios a moderarse. La OCDE advierte de que la inflación continuará siendo una fuente de presión para los hogares españoles y que seguirá situada claramente por encima de la media europea . El repunte del coste de la energía, especialmente de los carburantes, amenaza además con trasladarse progresivamente al resto de bienes y servicios, dificultando la recuperación del poder adquisitivo de las familias.

El último dato de inflación refleja precisamente ese cambio de escenario. El IPC se situó en agosto en el 4,3%, su nivel más elevado desde 2023, impulsado principalmente por el encarecimiento de los carburantes. La evolución de los precios introduce así un elemento de incertidumbre sobre la capacidad de los hogares para beneficiarse plenamente del crecimiento de la economía.

En su informe Perspectivas económicas de la OCDE: Superar sucesivas perturbaciones , el organismo dibuja de este modo una economía española que mantiene un mayor dinamismo que buena parte de Europa, pero que afronta al mismo tiempo una inflación todavía elevada.

España cerró 2025 con un crecimiento del 2,8% según los cálculos que maneja la OCDE, aunque esta cifra no incorpora todavía la revisión a la baja realizada recientemente por el INE, que situó el avance del PIB del pasado ejercicio en el 2,6%. Para 2026, el organismo internacional mantiene a España entre las economías más dinámicas de Europa, con una previsión de crecimiento del 2,6%, aunque anticipa una moderación hasta el 1,8% en 2027.

El principal respaldo de la economía española seguirá procediendo de la demanda interna, que mantuvo un comportamiento sólido durante el segundo trimestre. El consumo y la inversión continúan sosteniendo la actividad en un momento en el que el escenario exterior ofrece menos apoyo. El comercio internacional y la industria manufacturera están acusando el debilitamiento de la economía mundial y las mayores incertidumbres derivadas del contexto geopolítico.

La distancia con las principales economías europeas se mantiene amplia. La OCDE calcula que Alemania crecerá un 1,1% tanto en 2026 como en 2027, mientras que Francia apenas avanzará un 0,4% este año y un 0,7% el próximo. Italia, por su parte, registrará tasas del 0,9% y del 0,6%. En el conjunto de la zona euro, el crecimiento se quedará en torno al 1% en ambos ejercicios. Para las economías del G-20, las previsiones apuntan a avances del 3,1% en 2026 y del 3% en 2027.
sources.headline: La OCDE mejora en cuatro décimas la previsión de crecimiento de España en 2026, pero advierte de que la inflación seguirá por encima de la media europea

stories.headline: Barcelona's Fabra i Puig commuter-rail station remains closed after ceiling collapse injures three

sources.body:
Rodalies afronta este miércoles una jornada complicada, con varias incidencias que afectan al servicio. La principal se encuentra en Fabra i Puig, donde este martes por la tarde se desprendió parte del falso techo del vestíbulo de la estación y tres personas resultaron heridas. La estación permanece cerrada y los trenes no efectúan parada hasta nuevo aviso.

En este directo de EL PERIÓDICO seguimos minuto a minuto la evolución del servicio y las afectaciones a los viajeros.

Una incidencia en la infraestructura entre Sant Vicenç de Calders y Vilanova i la Geltrú afecta a seis líneas de Rodalies. La R2 Sud, R13, R14, R15, R16 y R17 circulan con demoras que pueden superar los 20 minutos.

Además, algunos trenes acumulan retrasos mayores. Un R15 procedente de Móra la Nova y con destino Barcelona Estació de França circula con 62 minutos de demora, mientras que un R17 entre Barcelona y Salou-PortAventura acumula 28 minutos.

La afectación se suma a las incidencias que ya se registraban esta mañana en otros puntos de la red.

La incidencia que está afectando este miércoles a la R1 entre Badalona y El Clot se debe a un nuevo robo de cable de cobre .

El corte de cable ha afectado a la señalización de este tramo. Personal de Adif trabaja para reparar la avería y recuperar la circulación con normalidad.

La R2 Sud registra retrasos este miércoles por una incidencia en la señalización en Cunit. La afectación alcanza tanto a los trenes de Rodalies como a los servicios de Media Distancia.

Personal de Adif trabaja en la zona para resolver la incidencia y recuperar la circulación con normalidad.

Además de la afectación en Fabra i Puig, varias líneas acumulan retrasos esta mañana. La R11 registra 55 minutos de demora por una incidencia técnica del tren, mientras que la R14 circula con 37 minutos de retraso y la R15, con 26 minutos por incidencias en la infraestructura.

La R2 Sud también registra retrasos que pueden superar los 20 minutos entre Sant Vicenç de Calders y Vilanova i la Geltrú. En la RL3, un tren circula con 25 minutos de demora por una incidencia operativa.

La estación de Fabra i Puig continúa cerrada este miércoles después de que este martes por la tarde se desprendiera parte del falso techo del vestíbulo. Tres personas resultaron heridas leves y fueron trasladadas al Hospital Vall d’Hebron.

Los trenes de la R4 mantienen la circulación, pero no efectúan parada en la estación hasta nuevo aviso. Los viajeros pueden bajar en La Sagrera-Meridiana y continuar hasta Fabra i Puig con la línea 1 de Metro, con los billetes y abonos de Rodalies habilitados para este transbordo.

Por el momento, no hay previsión de reapertura de la estación.

La R3 mantiene el transporte alternativo por carretera entre La Molina y Puigcerdà y La Tor de Querol debido a una incidencia en la infraestructura.

La afectación, comunicada por Rodalies a las 06.55 horas, continúa activa.

El servicio de Rodalies suma nuevas incidencias este miércoles por la mañana. Los problemas afectan ahora a varias líneas, con retrasos que llegan a los 55 minutos en la R11 .

stories.headline: Catalan president Illa acknowledges serious errors in the latest PISA assessment process

sources.body:
El president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa , ha admès que les proves PISA 2025 van incloure "errors greus i inacceptables" per per l'exempció d'un percentatge d'alumnes (23,2%) molt superior al màxim que recomana l'OCDE (5%), i ha apuntat al Consell d'Avaluació per no informar bé els centres.

Ho ha dit aquest dimecres en una compareixença al Parlament, a petició pròpia, que també havien sol·licitat Junts, Esquerra, els Comuns, Vox i la CUP.

Segons ha detallat, l'INE va avisar que hi havia massa alumnes exempts l'abril de l'any passat amb les proves en marxa, advertència que "no va arribar als centres" tot i que n'hi havia que encara no havien fet les proves.

Illa ha apuntat també que, durant les setmanes següents, el Consell d'Avaluació va rebre sis informes tècnics i que, arran d'això, s'hauria d'haver reforçat el seguiment i advertir els centres, així com extremar la supervisió de les exempcions.

A més, ha revelat que la informació sobre aquesta incidència no va arribar als responsables polítics del Departament d'Educació. No va ser fins al febrer del 2026, quan es van rebre els resultats de les proves, que l'error va arribar als càrrecs polítics.

El sistema no va funcionar com havia de funcionar, hi va haver errors d'interpretació, errors de supervisió i mancances en la transmissió d'informació rellevant.

Per tot plegat, a l'agost Educació va rellevar la secretària general del departament i va obrir una investigació, que va derivar en tres expedients disciplinaris , com ha recordat Illa en la compareixença al Parlament.

"No correspon identificar les persones. Seran els expedients els que determinaran els fets, les responsabilitats individuals i les conseqüències que se'n derivin", ha dit el president.

En el seu discurs, ha advertit que no s'han perdut les proves i que no s'han manipulat resultats sinó que es tracta d'un problema metodològic que fa que els resultats no siguin representatius.

L'error es va fer públic aquest juliol . La Generalitat llavors ho va considerar una "incidència tècnica" i va dir que n'investigaria les causes. La consellera Esther Niubó en va exculpar els directors dels centres, després d'haver atribuït l'error a la coincidència en el temps amb les proves de 4t d'ESO.

En el debat al Parlament, la portaveu de Junts, Mònica Sales, ha demanat la destitució de la consellera d'Educació, i ha acusat el govern de "manipular la mostra" i "amagar l'escàndol fins que no van poder més":

Han convertit Catalunya en la riota de PISA.

"Aquest error ha portat el país al ridícul" , ha dit al seu torn el portaveu d'ERC, Jordi Albert, que ha dit que la dimensió de l'error "és enorme" i que el govern ho sabia des de molt abans: "han tingut una actitud d'opacitat volguda ". Per això, ha reclamat responsabilitats polítiques.

Per Alejandro Fernández (PP), amb l'escàndol de les PISA, Illa ha convertit el sistema educatiu en " la riota d'Europa " després "d'ocultar deliberadament les dades". I ha dit que tant el president com la consellera Niubó en són responsables.
sources.headline: Illa admet errors greus en el fiasco de PISA i apunta al Consell d'Avaluació per no informar bé els centres

sources.body:
Salvador Illa compareció este miércoles en el Parlament para explicar por qué los resultados de las pruebas PISA en Catalunya han quedado invalidados, pero dejó sin aclarar las principales incógnitas del fiasco: por qué se excluyó de la evaluación a más del 23% de los alumnos seleccionados, todos ellos estudiantes con dificultades, y por qué la conselleria de Educació ignoró los siete avisos del Instituto Nacional de Evaluación Educativa para corregir la situación. El president se limitó a repetir ante la oposición el relato que ya expuso la consellera Esther Niubó el pasado 31 de agosto sobre una crisis que, por ahora, se ha saldado con el relevo de la número dos del Departament y la apertura de tres expedientes disciplinarios.

Illa ha defendido que el "no estamos hablando de una alteración de los resultados ni de un problema en la corrección", "ni se han perdido los exámenes", "hablamos de un error grave en el proceso de aplicación de las pruebas ", ha apuntado el president. Un "error" que afectó directamente a qué alumnos hacían las pruebas y, por tanto, a la representatividad de los resultados. Catalunya dejó fuera de la evaluación a más del 23% de los estudiantes seleccionados , una proporción que multiplica por más de cuatro el máximo del 5% admitido por la OCDE . De los 2.545 alumnos de 15 años pertenecientes a los 51 centros de la muestra, 591 no llegaron a examinarse: seis por una discapacidad física; 493 por necesidades de apoyo relacionadas con dificultades "cognitivas, conductuales o emocionales"; y 92 por un dominio insuficiente de la lengua. S olo cinco de los 51 centros hicieron bien la muestra.

Como ya hizo Niubó , el president ha explicado en el Parlament que se han incoado expedientes disciplinarios a tres personas. Estas -aunque Illa no lo ha especificado- son dos funcionarias de la conselleria que trabajaban en el desaparecido Consell Superior d'Avaluació que podrían haber incurrido en un presunto incumplimiento grave de sus obligaciones y deberes como funcionarios públicos, y a un exalto cargo de la conselleria , que podría haber incurrido, presuntamente, "en una infracción leve por actos y omisiones" que constituyen "descuido o negligencia ". ¿La negligencia? Hacer caso omiso a las siete advertencias del Instituto Nacional de Evaluación Educativa (INEE) del error en la muestra en a bril de 2025, cuando las pruebas aún se estaban realizando y había "margen de maniobra".

Tras la explicación del "error" de PISA -que Illa ha tildado de "inaceptable" y ha señalado que " no tendría que haber pasado "- el president ha insistido -como ya hizo también Niubó- en que la información sobre esta "incidencia" no fue elevada a los responsables políticos del Departament hasta febrero del 2026, cuando la actual directora de la Agència d'Avaluació i Prospectiva de l'Educació [organismo que sustituye al desaparecido Consell Superior d'Avaluació] recibió una "comunicación oral del error" y, ella sí, lo elevó al director general de currículum, y fue cuando empezó la investigación interna que determinó la incoación de los tres expedientes disciplinarios.

stories.headline: Barcelona bus workers plan further strike action unless an agreement with TMB is reached

sources.body:
La vaga dels conductors d’autobús de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) no serà flor d’un dia. Els treballadors del servei han acordat a l’ assemblea general de treballadors celebrada aquest dimarts al migdia a les cotxeres de Sants la convocatòria de més mobilitzacions si no hi ha canvis en la negociació del nou conveni col·lectiu . Les aturades seran parcials, de dues hores per torn . És a dir, un total de sis hores per dia durant tota la setmana. Aquestes afectacions es faran efectives en un màxim de dues setmanes, de manera que podrien produir-se a mitjans del pròxim mes d’octubre. La mesura s’adopta després que aquesta part de la plantilla de l’operador metropolità hagi protagonizat avui una primera jornada de vaga de set hores , des de les deu del matí fins a les cinc de la tarda.

TMB tindrà ara dues setmanes per provar d’evitar noves mobilitzacions dels seus empleats, tal com ja es va intentar aquest dilluns a última hora amb fins a quatre reunions de mediació que van resultar infructuoses. Cal recordar que les reivindicacions parteixen de la necessitat de conciliar la vida laboral i familiar treballant menys temps, unes reivindicacions que s’allarguen des de finals del 2025 i per les quals hi ha hagut 23 trobades entre les parts sense acord. Per fer-ho, demanen més contractació per poder repartir les tasques entre més personal. “L’aplicació de les 35 hores i uns descansos, coherents amb el segle en què vivim, permetrà un millor servei que repercutirà en la seguretat de la societat barcelonina, amb personal de conducció descansat i sense una afectació greu de l’estrès inherent a la difícil circulació d’aquesta ciutat”, apunten els treballadors. I afegeixen: “Les mobilitzacions són per necessitat, ja que la càrrega de treball cada vegada és major en tots els col·lectius. No entenem que una empresa pública es gestioni per rendiments econòmics, i no per garantir el servei públic de transport”.

La Generalitat havia fixat aquest dimarts uns serveis mínims del 20% al bus de Barcelona entre les deu del matí i les quatre de la tarda i del 40% entre les quatre i les cinc de la tarda, quan la vaga coincidia amb l’hora punta. També s’havia de garantir un bus de barri per línia i el personal indispensable per mantenir les infraestructures necessàries per al funcionament dels serveis mínims i el reinici de la circulació.
sources.headline: Els conductors de bus de TMB convoquen noves aturades parcials

sources.body:
Un autobús de la línea V29 de Barcelona. / AYUNTAMIENTO DE BARCELONA / EUROPA PRESS

Los trabajadores de los autobuses de Barcelona volverán a convocar paros parciales a principios de octubre si en los próximos 15 días no alcanzan un acuerdo con Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) para cerrar el nuevo convenio laboral que lleva estancado desde noviembre de 2025.

Así lo han decidido los empleados en una asamblea general extraordinaria celebrada esta mañana en las Cotxeres de Sants, que ha servido para explicar a la plantilla la situación y para decidir bajo voto las próximas movilizaciones que seguirán a la de este martes. En la reunión, la plantilla ha acordado realizar otro paro parcial entre los días 5 y 9 de noviembre como medida de presión si no hay un pacto con una propuesta "satisfactoria" para todas las partes.

Para alcanzar un acuerdo con la dirección, el comité insiste en que una de las principales reivindicaciones del colectivo es la reducción de la jornada laboral a 35 horas semanales , además de establecer unos descansos "coherentes con el siglo en el que vivimos" y el cumplimiento de los dos días consecutivo de descanso a la semana.

Los representantes de los trabajadores sostienen que estas medidas permitirían mejorar el servicio al garantizar que los conductores afronten su jornada en mejores condiciones y reducir el impacto del "estrés inherente " a la compleja circulación de Barcelona. Además, según señalan en un comunicado, " las reivindicaciones son claras " y responden a la necesidad de facilitar la conciliación de la vida laboral y familiar mediante una reducción del tiempo de trabajo.

Este martes Barcelona ha presenciado un paro desde las diez de la mañana que ha dejado afectada la frecuencia de los autobuses gestionados por TMB, reducida al 20% del servicio hasta las cuatro de la tarde. En la última hora de la jornada de huelga, hasta las 17 horas de la tarde, se ha ampliado la frecuencia hasta un 40% al coincidir con hora punta por la salida en las escuelas y se ha mantenido un bus de barrio por línea durante toda la convocatoria.

La huelga vino motivada tras diez meses de negociaciones y 23 reuniones sin acuerdo para cerrar el nuevo convenio laboral. Antes del paro, ambas partes se habían encontrado en cuatro reuniones de mediación en el Departament de Treball, donde se acercaron las posturas pero no se llegó a ningún acuerdo favorable.

Sin embargo, " en cuatro días no se puede arreglar lo que se ha negociado durante 11 meses sin resultado ", ha recriminado el presidente del comité de empresa de TMB, Jesús Linares, en declaraciones a ACN. "Esperemos que en estos 15 días de margen la empresa lleve una propuesta definitiva que pueda ser analizada por toda la plantilla y se pueda votar", ha explicado.

Desde TMB han cifrado en un 68% el seguimiento de la huelga , realizado para facilitar la asistencia de los trabajadores a la asamblea, y ha asegurado que se han cumplido los servicios mínimos sin incidencias. Por otro lado, reitera que siguen comprometidos para llegar a un acuerdo lo antes posible con el colectivo.

stories.headline: Barcelona begins La Mercè festival with expanded venues and a beachside piromusical

sources.body:
Imagen del Correfoc de las fiestas de la Mercè de 2025. / MANU MITRU / EPC

Sin precisión matemática, pero con la información que trae el ambiente que se vive en la ciudad, se puede afirmar que las fiestas de la Mercè llegan cuando las vacaciones ya llevan días, semanas, extinguidas. Con ello, el dolor por la pérdida del ocio ya ha remitido de forma considerable y uno se hace a la idea de que toca volver al redil, al colegio, al trabajo. Las fiestas de Barcelona empiezan en ese punto de relajación resignada, y este año lo harán de la mano de un hombre que decidió que su empresa principal sería demostrar que el vino podía ser mejor y además hecho aquí mismo.

Toni Falgueras , el alma del Celler de Gelida , abrirá este miércoles por la tarde los fastos barceloneses de este 2026 de la mano de su hija: rechazó el honor si le tocaba asumirlo en solitario, pero encontró en Meritxell su media naranja con vocación mediática. Padre e hija darán, pues, el pistoletazo de salida a la fiesta el miércoles por la tarde en el Saló de Cent, al pronunciar el pregón, en un acto que sin duda será un homenaje al buen vino, el catalán pero no solamente, y al comercio histórico en su conjunto, que por algo el Celler tiene ya 131 años de historia y la quinta generación al frente.

Barcelona acogerá del 23 al 27, es decir, de este miércoles al domingo, todo tipo de espectáculos gratuitos al aire libre. En resumen y con cifras: la programación llegará a los diez distritos en 32 espacios, un total de 109 conciertos, 55 actuaciones de cultura popular y 180 funciones de artes de calle. Hay clásicos que no conviene olvidar: de los gegants al Correfoc, que el día 26 llenará el paseo de Gràcia: 600 metros a fuego vivo entre Provença y Consell de Cent. El Correfoc de La Mercè estrena nueva Puerta del Infierno . 14 metros de ancho --todo el del paseo de Gràcia-- y siete de altura. Mil cuerpos fragmentados obra de Daniel Esteban “que aluden --comparan-- a la fuerza de la cultura popular”.

Una de las diferencias que los barceloneses notarán este año es la aparición de nuevos escenarios y el cambio de otros. La plaza de las Glòries será, tras tantas décadas de acoger esencialmente asfalto y neumático, la gran novedad : contará este 2026 con actividades para todos los públicos de 11.00 a 19.30 horas, en seis zonas de actividades. Allí tendrá lugar el jueves la primera sesión del festival Mercè Arts de Carrer (MAC) que repartirá su arte por toda la ciudad: 68 compañías, más de 200 artistas y 170 funciones gratuitas llenarán parques, plazas y paseos durante la Mercè. En el Fort Pienc, en el Parc de l'Estació del Nord, se verán las artes más experimentales, con actividades desde la mañana hasta la noche entre el 24 y el 27 de septiembre..

Sin duda, uno de los platos principales de la oferta de estos días es 'EMERGENCY EXIT', el nuevo espectáculo de gran formato de La Fura dels Baus, Eyesberg y Satori , que se representará el 24 de septiembre en el Moll de la Fusta . Se trata de una propuesta inmersiva que combinará teatro, música y recursos audiovisuales.
